title: Escrowed request stabilizer and end-to-end traceback runbook for hosted API 5xx waves
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
During a recent customer escalation (INC-2026-03-07) we observed a repeatable pattern: downstream runtime timeouts caused edge proxies to reissue requests, causing duplicated work, KV cache churn, and a self-amplifying 5xx wave for a subset of tenants. Existing mitigations (circuit breakers and tenant throttles) reduced worst-case latency but did not prevent transient storms when customer SDKs re-tried aggressively.

Goal:
1) Implement an "escrowed request stabilizer" shim at the edge/proxy layer that temporarily holds identical in-flight requests for a short dedupe window (configurable, default 250ms) and returns a single upstream call to the runtime while streaming results to waiting clients.
2) Add end-to-end traceback headers and sampling to correlate client->edge->runtime flows for rapid postmortem and live debug.
3) Ship an operator-friendly runbook and dashboard tiles to detect, pause, and safely roll back the stabilizer if it introduces regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Observability: >95% of deduped requests are visible in the new E2E trace view within 30s of occurrence.
- Stability: No >=P0 customer sees increased tail latency (p99) after the feature is enabled in canary tenants.
- Safety: Operator can disable stabilizer per-region or per-tenant within 2 minutes without pipeline restarts.
- Regression guard: Automated A/B comparison shows no increase in 5xx rate for canary group during 48h canary.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Dedup window: 250ms chosen based on request distribution analysis (median inter-arrival for duplicate keys ~120ms, 95th ~370ms). Short window reduces chance of masking legitimate independent requests but may miss longer-spaced retries; we will expose as config.
- Stream semantics: We will implement the stabilizer to proxy streaming responses as they arrive (no buffering of full response), minimizing latency for streaming workloads. This requires head-of-line management to prevent head-blocking in proxy worker threads; we will use a bounded async queue per key and backpressure hooks.
- Consistency: The shim only dedupes requests with identical immutable inputs (model id, model version, prompt hash, routing metadata). We will not dedupe calls that include ephemeral tool-calls or function-calling contexts to avoid masking side effects.
- Failure modes: If upstream returns a non-idempotent status (e.g., 5xx accompanied by partial side-effects), the shim will not replicate the error to queued clients but will retry according to current retry policy. Operator-visible metric increments will indicate such events.

Implementation plan:
1) Proxy shim prototype in edge (Go): 2 sprint days to add key-based in-flight table, TTL, and async subscriber list.
2) Trace headers: add X-RW-Trace, X-RW-Trace-Sampled, and store mapping in trace DB for 7 days.
3) Runtime handshake: lightweight capability bit so runtime can indicate whether a request is safe to dedupe (backwards compatible).
4) Canary rollout: tenant-level flagging in control plane; start with internal tenants -> 5 low-volume customers -> broad canary cohort -> global.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for dedupe semantics, stream passthrough, and queue eviction.
- Load test with replayed tenant patterns from INC-2026-03-07; assert no increased worker CPU or memory >10%.
- Chaos tests: simulate upstream 5xx and partial responses to verify fail-open behavior.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Feature gate in control plane with per-tenant override. Default off.
- Enable for internal tenants (2h observation), then 5 canary customers (48h), then ramp to 20% traffic for 72h with automated metrics checks.
- Immediate rollback: control plane toggle to disable feature for a tenant/region. Post-mortem steps documented below.

Runbook summary (for on-call):
- Detect: new dashboard tile "Escrow stabilizer dedupe rate" + alert if dedupe_rate > 1% and associated p99 > baseline+20%.
- Triage: check trace sampler for correlated X-RW-Trace IDs, inspect proxy per-key queue sizes.
- Mitigate: toggle feature off for affected tenant(s); if not effective, kill per-proxy worker pool via safe drain (avoid global restart).
- Postmortem: collect trace IDs, edge logs, runtime logs, and set follow-up ENG ticket with timeline and fix suggestions.
